author: ali-ahmad

fields.hint: Units used in peak hours this month: the peak reading on a ToU bill.

fields.name: offpeak_units
fields.label: Off-peak units
fields.hint: Units used in all other hours: the off-peak reading on the bill.

fields.label: Sanctioned load
fields.hint: The kW printed on the bill. ToU meters are fitted to domestic connections of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW and above; below that, use the [[F1|electricity bill calculator]].

fields.label: MDI (maximum demand)
fields.hint: The MDI reading on the bill, if shown. Leave blank if your bill has none; the fixed charge then uses half the sanctioned load.

fields.label: Billing quarter for QTA
fields.hint: The quarterly tariff adjustment depends on the quarter the bill falls in.

fields.name: fpa_per_unit
fields.label: FPA / FCA
fields.hint: Pre-filled with the latest NEPRA-verified fuel adjustment, the one for {{data.fpa_latest.fpa_for}} charged on {{data.fpa_latest.label}} bills. {{data.fpa_newest.note}} Replace it with the rate printed on your bill (negative is a credit).

fields.name: fpa_units
fields.label: Units in the FPA month
fields.hint: NEPRA charges the FPA on the units of the month it adjusts (the FPA month, usually two months before this bill), not on this month's units. Copy that month's units from the units history on your bill. Blank = this month's units.

fields.name: fc_surcharge_per_unit
fields.label: FC surcharge
fields.hint: Financing cost surcharge per unit, from your bill. Secondary-source default; change it if your bill differs.

fields.name: gst_pct
fields.label: GST
fields.hint: Sales tax applied to the bill subtotal.

answer: Peak hours for LESCO and the other ex-WAPDA DISCOs are {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.months}} and {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}}, per NEPRA's 2023 IESCO schedule, not yet re-confirmed for 2026. On a time-of-use meter ({{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW and above) {{out.units|int}} units cost about {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
how: Energy: {{out.energy_calc}} (peak + off-peak) = {{out.energy_rs|rs}} for {{out.units|int}} units. Fixed charge: billed on {{out.billable_kw|1}} kW, the higher of half the {{out.sanctioned_kw|1}} kW sanctioned load and the MDI entered ({{out.mdi_kw|1}} kW) = {{out.fixed_rs|rs}}. FC surcharge {{out.fc_rs|rs}}, QTA {{out.qta_rs|rs}}, FPA {{out.fpa_rs|rs}}. Subtotal {{out.subtotal_rs|rs}}; GST at {{out.gst_pct}}% = {{out.gst_rs|rs}}. Estimated bill {{out.total_rs|rs}}.
key_facts: Under the latest NEPRA schedule found (the 2023 IESCO tariff determination; PITC's bill portal confirms only the {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}} window), peak hours are {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}} and {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.months}}; every other hour is off-peak.

Peak hours change the price only on a time-of-use (ToU) meter, which domestic connections of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load or more must have; smaller connections pay the normal slab rate at any hour.

On the A-1 domestic ToU tariff a peak unit costs {{data.tariff.tou.peak|rs2}} and an off-peak unit {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}}, so every unit moved out of peak hours saves the difference between the two.

A ToU home using {{out.peak_units|int}} peak and {{out.offpeak_units|int}} off-peak units pays {{out.energy_rs|rs}} in energy charges and about {{out.total_rs|rs}} in all with the fixed charge, FC surcharge, QTA, FPA and GST; with only {{ex.1.in.peak_units|int}} of the same units in peak hours the bill falls to {{ex.1.out.total_rs|rs}}.
K-Electric publishes its own peak-hour timings, so Karachi consumers should check K-Electric's schedule rather than the DISCO one; the rates and the fuel adjustment are the same uniform figures.

Income tax is not in this estimate: under section 235 of the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, a home not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays advance income tax of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more; consumers on the list pay none.

formula.text: ToU bill = peak units × peak rate + off-peak units × off-peak rate + fixed rate per kW × max(half the sanctioned load, MDI) + (FC + QTA + FPA) × units, then + GST
lines: peak and off-peak rates = A-1 domestic ToU rates in the NEPRA tariff (data/tariff-pk-2026.json)
peak window = the season's peak hours; every other hour is off-peak
MDI = maximum demand indicator reading in kW
FC surcharge, QTA and FPA per unit and GST on the subtotal, as on the flat bill (whole rupees per line)

p: The latest peak-hour schedule we could find on NEPRA's site is the one in its 2023 tariff determination for IESCO. The PITC bill portal (the billing system the government DISCOs share) currently shows only the {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}} window, which matches it; the other three seasons below come from the 2023 determination alone. It gives four seasons, each with a {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.hours|int}}-hour evening peak.

{{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}}: peak {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}}. {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.months}}: peak {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.to}}. {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}}: peak {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}}. {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.months}}: peak {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.to}}.

This schedule has not been re-confirmed for 2026. An August 2025 news report said NEPRA asked the DISCOs to propose peak hours ending no later than eleven at night; we have not found a decision adopting a new schedule. The time printed on your own ToU bill or your DISCO's notice overrides this page.

sections.h2: Peak hours IESCO, MEPCO and the other DISCOs
p: We expect the same schedule to apply to all ex-WAPDA DISCOs: LESCO, IESCO, MEPCO, GEPCO, FESCO, PESCO, HESCO, SEPCO, QESCO and TESCO. The 2023 determination we found is IESCO's, but the DISCOs bill through the same PITC system, which shows one {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}} window for all of them. That is an inference for the other seasons, not a published fact, so check the peak time printed on your own ToU bill.
K-Electric is the exception. It sets and publishes its own peak-hour timings for Karachi, so check K-Electric's schedule or your bill rather than the schedule above.

sections.h2: Off peak hours: when is electricity cheaper?
p: Every hour outside the peak window is off-peak: in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}} that means before {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} and after {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}}, the whole night and the whole day included. An off-peak unit costs {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}} against {{data.tariff.tou.peak|rs2}} for a peak unit on the domestic ToU tariff.

sections.h2: Peak hours in summer and winter
p: The peak moves with sunset. In summer ({{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}}) it is latest, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}}, when evening AC use is highest. In winter ({{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}}) it is earliest, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}}, when lights, heaters and geysers come on after dark. Spring and autumn sit in between.

sections.h2: Who pays peak rates: ToU meter rates explained
p: Only connections on a time-of-use meter. NEPRA's domestic tariff puts every connection with a sanctioned load of {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW or more on a ToU meter, which records peak and off-peak units separately. A smaller connection on a normal meter pays its slab rate whatever the hour, so shifting use to the night does not change its bill.

A ToU bill has two energy lines, peak units at {{data.tariff.tou.peak|rs2}} and off-peak units at {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}}, and a fixed charge of {{data.tariff.tou.fixed_per_kw|rs}} per kW on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI. The FC surcharge, quarterly adjustment, fuel adjustment and GST are added after that, as on any bill.

sections.h2: How much you save by shifting AC, iron and motor use
p: Every unit moved out of the peak window saves the gap between {{data.tariff.tou.peak|rs2}} and {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}}. For the default month, {{out.peak_units|int}} peak and {{out.offpeak_units|int}} off-peak units carry an energy charge of {{out.energy_rs|rs}}; with only {{ex.1.in.peak_units|int}} units in the peak, the same total carries {{ex.1.out.energy_rs|rs}}, and GST on the gap makes the saving a little larger on the whole bill.

The easy moves: iron, run the washing machine and fill the water tank with the motor before the peak starts; pre-cool rooms before the peak and raise the AC set point by a degree or two during it; charge UPS batteries off-peak. The ToU calculator above shows the bill for your own peak and off-peak readings.

mistakes: Shifting use to the night on a normal meter. Below {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load the bill uses slab rates at every hour, so the time of use does not change the price.
Using another DISCO's or K-Electric's timings. K-Electric publishes its own schedule; check the time on your own bill.
Treating this schedule as confirmed for 2026. It is NEPRA's 2023 schedule; a newer one may apply, and your DISCO's notice overrides it.
Forgetting the fixed charge. On a ToU meter it is billed on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI, so a high evening MDI raises it too.
safety: Running the water motor, washing machine or geyser on a timer to beat the peak is fine, but timers and contactors on motor and geyser circuits must be rated for the load and fitted by a licensed electrician.

faq.q: What are the peak hours for LESCO in 2026?
faq.a: Under NEPRA's latest schedule found, from 2023: {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.1.months}}, {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}} and {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.3.months}}. It is not yet re-confirmed for 2026; check your bill.

faq.q: What are the peak hours for IESCO and MEPCO?
faq.a: Most likely the same as LESCO. The schedule here is from NEPRA's 2023 IESCO determination; the PITC bill portal, shared by all ex-WAPDA DISCOs, confirms only the {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}} window, so check your bill for the other seasons. By the 2023 schedule, in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.months}} the peak is {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.2.to}}.
Every hour outside the evening peak window, including the whole day and night. Off-peak units cost {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}} on the domestic ToU tariff.

faq.q: What are the peak hours in winter?
faq.a: {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.from}} to {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.to}} in {{data.tariff.tou.peak_hours.seasons.0.months}} under the 2023 schedule, the earliest window of the year.

faq.q: What are the ToU meter rates?
faq.a: {{data.tariff.tou.peak|rs2}} per peak unit and {{data.tariff.tou.offpeak|rs2}} per off-peak unit on the A-1 domestic tariff, plus a fixed charge of {{data.tariff.tou.fixed_per_kw|rs}} per kW on the higher of half the sanctioned load and the MDI.

faq.q: Do peak hours matter if I do not have a ToU meter?
faq.a: No. Below {{d.tou_threshold_kw|int}} kW sanctioned load the bill is worked out on slab rates whatever the time, so use the [[F1|electricity bill calculator]] instead.
K-Electric publishes its own peak-hour timings, so check its schedule or your Karachi bill rather than the DISCO schedule on this page.

faq.q: Why is my real bill higher than this estimate when it is over {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}}?
faq.a: Usually because of advance income tax, which this estimate leaves out: a domestic consumer not on FBR's Active Taxpayers List pays {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.rate_pct_non_atl|1}}% on a monthly bill of {{data.tariff.addons_secondary.income_tax_235.threshold_rs|rs}} or more. [[F1|Who pays the income tax line]] is explained with the electricity bill calculator.
